diagram:
flowchart TD
  SCHED["⏰ pg_cron per market
US 14:05 UTC · India 11:05 UTC"] --> PICK["📥 pending · direction='long'
≥ mandate score_threshold · deterministic_v1 only"]
  PICK --> GATES{"🛡️ Deterministic gate stack
kill-switch · pause · blocklist · sector · cooldown"}
  GATES -->|"blocked"| REJECT["⏭️ Rejected
pipeline_stage_events + decision_journal"]
  GATES -->|"passes"| CAPS["🔢 mandate.max_open_positions
per market · Settings-editable · default 10"]
  CAPS --> KELLY["📐 Half-Kelly sizing
f = (p·b − (1−p)) / b"]
  KELLY --> FILL["💰 execute_paper_fill RPC
direct — no approval step exists"]

SCHED.label: pg_cron per market
SCHED.description: TWO per-market pg_cron jobs, not one: 'kairos-paper-trade-us' 5 14 * * 1-5 (10:05 ET) and 'kairos-paper-trade-india' 5 11 * * 1-5 (16:35 IST). Also still tail-chained from the research cron as a deliberate backstop. Deterministic — NOT an LLM. This is a Flow, not an AI agent. Note the route path is /api/agents/paper-trade; /api/agents/paper-trader is only an alias.
SCHED.addReason: Act on fresh signals shortly after open.
SCHED.changeReason: Schedule was wrong (9:45 AM single job → two per-market pg_cron jobs at 10:05 ET / 16:35 IST). 'Deterministic, not an LLM' verified accurate and kept.

PICK.label: Select signals
PICK.description: Selects agent_signals that are status='pending', direction='long', at or above the MANDATE's per-market score_threshold (60 is only the fallback default — presets: short_swing 65, swing 60, position 58), newer than a freshness cutoff, and score_source='deterministic_v1' as a positive allowlist. Signals older than the cutoff are marked status='expired' — that expiry is of stale SIGNALS, not of proposals. strategy_config.score_threshold is still read but is display/back-compat only and must never loosen a mandate.
PICK.addReason: Score threshold gates which signals become trades.
PICK.changeReason: '≥60' is a fallback default, not the rule; the threshold is mandate-driven per market. The direction, freshness, and score_source filters were all undrawn.

GATES.label: Deterministic gate stack
GATES.description: Rule-based, no LLM — but far more than 'size caps, exposure, rules'. In order: per-market kill-switch, market pause / trading-disabled, market-local trading-day freshness, score_source allowlist, symbol blocklist, sector cap, re-entry cooldown, per-trade and daily notional caps, asset-allocation gross-cap tightening, and a pyramid gate on adds. Rejections are recorded to pipeline_stage_events and decision_journal — there is no risk_check_reasons table.
GATES.addReason: Safety must be deterministic, never probabilistic.
GATES.changeReason: The node named a table that does not exist (risk_check_reasons) and described three checks where eleven run. Rejection reasons go to pipeline_stage_events + decision_journal.

REJECT.label: Rejected
REJECT.description: A blocked candidate is journalled with its reason rather than silently dropped, so a zero-fill day is explainable.
REJECT.addReason: Replaces the fictional 'skipped / expires' proposal branch with the reject path that actually exists.

CAPS.label: Mandate position cap
CAPS.description: Max open positions is config-driven from trading_mandates.max_open_positions — per market, Settings-editable, clamped 1-50, default 10 — and is enforced both in the route and again inside the fill RPC. It is not a hardcoded constant.
CAPS.addReason: Shipped since 2026-07-04 and undrawn; it is the cap a reader is most likely to want to change, and it now lives in Settings rather than in code.

KELLY.label: Half-Kelly sizing
KELLY.description: Standard Kelly: f = (p·b − (1−p)) / b, halved. Cap and floor come from the champion GENOME's sizing block, with the cap additionally clamped to the owner's positionSizePct — not a static 2% floor. Falls back to flat sizing when the calibrated pwin model or the MAE/MFE percentiles are absent, which is a data-availability condition, not a closed-trade count.
KELLY.addReason: Kelly sizes to edge; half-Kelly reduces variance; flat fallback avoids overfitting tiny samples.
KELLY.changeReason: The formula on the diagram was not the implemented one, the caps are genome-driven rather than static, and the flat-sizing fallback triggers on missing model artifacts rather than on '<10 closed trades'.

FILL.label: execute_paper_fill
FILL.description: Qualifying candidates are filled DIRECTLY via the execute_paper_fill RPC (transactional). There is no proposal row, no approval prompt, and no human step between a signal and a paper fill. Long-only is enforced by the direction='long' filter upstream. Also runs the Portfolio Constructor and capital rotation, and syncs benchmark/alpha.
FILL.addReason: Single authorized live account; everything else read-only.
FILL.changeReason: The diagram gated this behind a human approval of a trader_proposals row. Neither exists in the route — fills are direct via RPC.

POOLS.label: Per-market pools
POOLS.description: Fully separated per market: starting NAV US $10,000 / India ₹1,000,000, currency USD vs INR, and per-market kill-switch, pause, mandate, genome, and cutoff. The two NAVs are never summed.
POOLS.addReason: Multi-market shipped in migrations 057/058 and the diagram still described a single implicitly-US pool.

NOLIVE.label: Paper only
NOLIVE.description: This route contains no account id, no broker, and no live order path — it fills virtual long-only trades from qualifying signals. The locked rule that live orders may only ever come from account 605420660 remains true of the system, but it is enforced elsewhere; stating it here implied this flow can place real orders, which it cannot.
NOLIVE.addReason: Replaces the old FILL node's 'or live: acct 605420660' claim with the route's actual scope.

history.label: trader_proposals does not exist — the entire approval branch was fiction
history.reason: THE most serious falsehood found in this audit, and the reason it outranks every other correction on this page: the diagram told the owner that a human approval gate stands between a signal and a fill. It does not. 'trader_proposals' appears in ZERO route code — the only hits repo-wide are this diagram, a plan .md, AgentsPage.tsx, and WORK_LOG.md. app/api/agents/paper-trade/route.ts fills directly via the execute_paper_fill RPC. There is no proposal row, no approval prompt, no reminder job, and no human step. This is the exact defect class the 2026-07-16/17 batch exists to delete — a surface asserting a control that the data cannot support — except pointed at the safety story itself, which is the worst possible place for it. A reader trusting this diagram would believe they had a veto they have never had. Removed rather than edited because no amount of rewording preserves a node for a control that was never built. NOTE the mitigating truth, established separately: this route is PAPER-ONLY (no account id, no broker, no live order path), so the missing gate has never let a real order through. The locked 'cron cannot approve/reject' and 'live orders only from 605420660' rules remain true of the SYSTEM and are enforced elsewhere — they were simply never true of this node.

history.label: 'Human approves?' decision node removed with the proposal branch
history.reason: Same root cause as PROP: the node drew a branch point the code does not contain. Removed rather than kept as a 'removed'-status node, because leaving a human-approval box on a safety diagram — greyed out or not — invites exactly the misreading it caused for two weeks. The real branch at this point in the flow is the deterministic gate stack (pass → fill, blocked → journalled reject), now drawn as GATES/REJECT.

history.label: 'Unapproved proposals expire; the reminder job nudges you' — none of that runs
history.reason: Removed with the rest of the approval fiction. There is no proposal to expire and no proposal-reminder job. The word 'expire' does map to something real, but to a different object entirely: the route marks stale SIGNALS status='expired' when they fall past the freshness cutoff — that behaviour has moved onto the PICK node where it belongs. The genuine skip path is a gate rejection, journalled to pipeline_stage_events + decision_journal, now drawn as REJECT.

history.label: Fills are direct via execute_paper_fill RPC; this route has no live path at all
history.reason: Two corrections. (1) The fill is unconditional on any human step — execute_paper_fill is called directly and transactionally the moment the gates pass. (2) 'Paper fills always; live orders only ever from account 605420660 … when trading_mode is enabled' put a live-order capability on a route that has none: no account id, no broker, no order call, and a header comment stating it fills virtual long-only trades. Splitting that into the NOLIVE node matters in both directions — it stops the diagram implying this cron can reach real money, and it stops a reader thinking 605420660's protection is what keeps it from doing so. Also recorded the Portfolio Constructor, capital rotation, and benchmark/alpha sync that run here undrawn.

history.label: max_open_positions is mandate-driven (10/market, Settings-editable), not hardcoded
history.reason: Shipped since 2026-07-04, undrawn. The cap is read from trading_mandates.max_open_positions per market, clamped 1-50, defaulting to 10, and is enforced twice — once in the route and again inside the fill RPC as a defence in depth. Given its own node because it is the control a reader is most likely to want to change, and the diagram gave no hint that it now lives in Settings rather than in code. Per-market matters: the US and India caps are independent, so 10 does not mean 10 in total.

history.label: Two per-market pg_cron jobs at 10:05 ET / 16:35 IST — not one 9:45 AM job
history.reason: 'Weekday 9:45 AM' matched nothing. Real: kairos-paper-trade-us 5 14 * * 1-5 (10:05 ET) and kairos-paper-trade-india 5 11 * * 1-5 (16:35 IST), both pg_cron, plus a deliberate tail-chain from the research cron as a backstop. Neither appears in vercel.json, which carries only four unrelated crons — a reader looking there for the schedule, as the file name invites, would conclude this flow is not scheduled at all. Also recorded that the real route path is /api/agents/paper-trade and that /api/agents/paper-trader (the agentId and AGENTS.md's spelling) is only an alias. 'Deterministic — NOT an LLM. This is a Flow, not an AI agent' is verified accurate and deliberately kept verbatim.

history.label: Eleven gates, not three; and risk_check_reasons is not a table
history.reason: 'Rule-based checks (size caps, exposure, long-only) — reasons stored in risk_check_reasons' understated the stack and named a table that does not exist. Real gates: per-market kill-switch, market pause/trading-disabled, market-local trading-day freshness, score_source allowlist, symbol blocklist, sector cap, re-entry cooldown, per-trade notional cap, daily notional cap, asset-allocation gross-cap tightening, pyramid gate on adds. Rejections are journalled to pipeline_stage_events and decision_journal — anyone querying risk_check_reasons to find out why a trade did not fire would have found no such relation. 'Safety must be deterministic, never probabilistic' is verified accurate and unchanged; the gate stack has no LLM anywhere in it.

history.label: Wrong formula, wrong caps, wrong fallback trigger
history.reason: Three errors in one node, all shipped 2026-07-01 and never corrected. (1) Formula: the diagram's 'f = wr/avgLoss − lr/avgWin' is not the implemented expression and is not dimensionally Kelly; the code computes standard Kelly, f = (p·b − (1−p)) / b, then halves it. (2) Caps: 'capped at positionSizePct, floored at 2%' — cap and floor come from the champion GENOME's sizing block, with the cap clamped down to the owner's positionSizePct; the 2% floor is not a constant. This is a live coupling the diagram denied: promoting a challenger can change position SIZE, not just scoring weights. (3) Fallback: 'falls back to flat sizing if fewer than 10 closed trades' is a plausible-sounding rule that does not exist — the real condition is the absence of a calibrated pwin model artifact or MAE/MFE percentiles, a data-availability test, not a trade count. The 10-trade number appears to have been borrowed from the LearnerAgent's Phase 0 gate, which is a different gate on a different agent.

history.label: Per-market pools + per-currency — multi-market was never drawn
history.reason: Shipped in migrations 057/058 and absent from this diagram entirely. US and India run fully separated pools: starting NAV $10,000 vs ₹1,000,000, currency USD vs INR, with per-market kill-switch, pause, mandate, genome, and freshness cutoff, and the two NAVs are deliberately never summed. Drawn because every other number on this page — the position cap, the score threshold, the notional caps — is per-market, and a single-pool mental model silently halves the reader's understanding of the system's real exposure.
